text:
alicia: noticed a cluster of tiny requests showing very high per-token cost on the cost dashboard. billing vs cache signals disagree. anyone seen this?

mike: saw it on canary. small prompt sizes but billed_tokens inflated. looks tied to router cache namespace change.

sandeep: we switched shared prefetch attribution last sprint; could be double-counting.

judy: example id?

alicia: inv-2024-11-05-a7c. console snippet: token_count=8, billed_units=24, cache_ns=ns_v1, model=redwood-7b-q4

mike: router now appends tenant suffix (ns_v2). if writers still write ns_v1 readers miss; billing charges full decode and prefetches fail.

zach: ops-bot pulled sample: invocation shows cache_key ns_v1, router variant suffix-tenants, prefetch_attempts=1, success=0.

sandeep: we don't surface cache_namespace or prefetch outcome in cost card. proposal: add a sampled "cost inspector" that shows hashed_cache_key, cache_namespace_version, prefetch_attempts, prefetch_success, billed_tokens, model_sku. default off.

mike: telemetry budget: sample 0.05% org-wide, tenant override for enterprise, cap at 1%.

judy: privacy: never show raw prompt text; only hashes. audit who views inspector.

sandeep: API: internal endpoint /internal/debug/cost?invocation_id=<id> returns minimal fields, requires X-Internal-Debug. Router emits compact cache events to a sampled Kafka topic; billing remains source of truth.

zach: rollout: backend emit compact events behind flag, console UI behind flag, 0.05% sampling, tenant override, monitor topic for 72h. also run key-migration with shadow-reader for 48h.

alicia: I'll draft RFC with schema, sampling, privacy and ops runbook. reconvene Tue to review. :thumbsup:
